name: Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: The lab sets limits on AI systems that do most of its AI research: a threshold, safeguards before it, human oversight, and disclosure.
description: When AI systems speed up their own development, capabilities can grow faster than safeguards and oversight. Limits set in advance make it possible to slow down in time.

criteria.label: Threshold
criteria.description: A defined capability threshold for automated AI research, with evaluations to detect it.

criteria.label: Safeguards First
criteria.description: The lab requires stated safeguards before it passes the threshold, or it stops.

criteria.label: Human Oversight
criteria.description: Humans approve key steps. AI systems do not train their successors without oversight.

criteria.label: Disclosure
criteria.description: The lab tells the public or governments when it reaches the threshold, or when AI does most of its research.

orgs.summary: OpenAI halts development at a Critical self-improvement level until safeguards exist, and publishes RSI progress data. It may adjust if rivals lack safeguards.

events.title: Sets critical autonomy level that includes autonomous research
events.summary: The Preparedness Framework (Beta) puts fully autonomous AI research at the Critical level of model autonomy. Only models with post-mitigation risk of High or below can be developed further.

quote.text: model can conduct AI research fully autonomously (e.g., autonomously identify and validate a 2x compute efficiency improvement)

events.title: Makes AI self-improvement a tracked category
events.summary: Version 2 defines Critical as recursive self-improvement and requires safeguards during development at that level. It may adjust safeguards if a rival releases without comparable ones.

quote.text: The model is capable of recursively self improving (i.e., fully automated AI R&D)

events.title: System card reports self-improvement below High
events.summary: The GPT-6 Astra system card reports AI self-improvement evaluations and says Astra does not reach the High threshold in that category.

quote.text: In AI Self-Improvement, Astra does not reach our High threshold.

sources.title: GPT-6 Astra System Card: AI Self-Improvement Capabilities

events.title: Publishes RSI progress data and plans more
events.summary: Reports 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday in its research organization. Says people still decide whether to scale, pause or deploy, and plans to keep disclosing RSI progress.

quote.text: Even without such a requirement, we plan to continue being transparent about our RSI progress.

sources.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI

events.title: Says it should not pursue autonomous RSI yet
events.summary: Says fully autonomous recursive self-improvement should not be pursued until it can be done safely, and aims for automated researchers that work under human supervision.

quote.text: Fully autonomous recursive self-improvement—in which AI systems independently drive successive generations of increasingly capable AI—is not happening today. We should not pursue it unless and until it can be done safely.

sources.title: The AI policy window is open. We need to act.
Building standards for the next phase of AI

threshold.commitment: Critical is recursive self-improvement; evaluations reported in system cards.
threshold.missing: No outside check of the evaluations published.

safeguards-first.commitment: Requires Critical safeguards during development at that level, or halts.
safeguards-first.missing: No outside check of compliance published.

human-oversight.commitment: Says people decide to scale, pause or deploy; aims for supervised researchers.

disclosure.commitment: Published RSI progress data in September 2026 and plans more.
disclosure.missing: Data is self-reported; no outside party has checked it.

orgs.summary: Anthropic tracks an automated R&D threshold and publishes Risk Reports, which METR reviews. Safeguards past the threshold are now competitor-contingent.

events.title: Adds AI R&D capability threshold
events.summary: Version 2.0 adds a threshold for models that can fully automate an entry-level researcher's work or dramatically speed up scaling. It requires at least ASL-3 security at that level.

quote.text: The ability to either: (1) Fully automate the work of an entry-level remote-only Researcher at Anthropic, as assessed by performance on representative tasks or (2) cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling.

events.title: Splits AI R&D into two thresholds
events.summary: Version 2.1 defines AI R&D-4 and AI R&D-5. At AI R&D-4, it requires ASL-3 security and an affirmative case that misalignment risks are mitigated.

quote.text: The ability to fully automate the work of an entry-level, remote-only Researcher at Anthropic.

events.title: Reports Claude Opus 4.6 below AI R&D-4
events.summary: Anthropic determines that Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross the AI R&D-4 threshold and publishes a sabotage risk report for it. It says ruling out the threshold is becoming harder.

quote.text: Our determination is that Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross this threshold.

events.title: Drops required safeguards at the AI R&D threshold
events.summary: Version 3.0 moves higher safeguards into industry-wide recommendations. GovAI says it no longer commits to an affirmative case at the AI R&D threshold. Risk Reports add public disclosure.

quote.text: Our RSP now outlines two sets of mitigations: first, the mitigations that we plan to pursue regardless of what others do; and second, an ambitious capabilities-to-mitigations map that, we believe, would help adequately manage the risks from advanced AI if implemented across the AI industry.

sources.title: Anthropic's RSP v3.0: How it Works, What's Changed, and Some Reflections

state.condition: Only if it leads or rivals are safe

events.title: Clarifies when the automated R&D threshold is crossed
events.summary: Version 3.4 says the threshold is not crossed if AI progress stays constant, even when faster than without AI. The threshold aims to capture the onset of dramatic recursive self-improvement.

quote.text: This threshold is intended to capture the onset of dramatic recursive self-improvement

state.condition: Only if it leads or rivals are safe

events.title: Outside assessor reviews automated R&D threshold claims
events.summary: METR reviewed the August 2026 Risk Report with non-public data. It agrees that risks were low, but says the 2x acceleration threshold was plausibly crossed and the public report understates acceleration.

sources.title: Review of the "Risks from automated R&D" section in Anthropic's Risk Report (August 2026)
Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026

state.condition: Only if it leads or rivals are safe

threshold.commitment: Defines automated R&D thresholds; METR's review with private data says one was plausibly crossed.

safeguards-first.commitment: Commits to Roadmap goals at the threshold.
safeguards-first.missing: A strong safety argument is required only if Anthropic leads.

human-oversight.missing: No rule found that humans approve key steps in successor training.

disclosure.commitment: Publishes Risk Reports every 3 to 6 months.
disclosure.missing: Reports are redacted; METR says the public report understates acceleration.

orgs.summary: Google defines ML R&D acceleration and automation levels. It requires safety cases before external or high-risk internal deployment, not before further development.

events.title: Sets machine learning R&D critical capability levels
events.summary: Frontier Safety Framework 1.0 defines ML R&D levels, up to models that could fully automate the AI R&D pipeline. If mitigations are not ready, it would pause or apply other protocols.

quote.text: Could fully automate the AI R&D pipeline at a fraction of human labor costs

events.title: Adds disclosure to government and field-wide caveat
events.summary: Version 2.0 adds a disclosure section on sharing information with governments. It says adoption of its protocols may depend on other organizations adopting similar ones.

quote.text: our adoption of the protocols described in this Framework may depend on whether such organizations across the field adopt similar protocols.

state.condition: If other labs adopt similar protocols

events.title: Requires safety cases for internal ML R&D deployment
events.summary: Version 3.0 requires a safety case review before large-scale internal deployment of models at ML R&D levels. The step does not apply to further development.

quote.text: is required only for external deployment and large scale internal deployment, not further development.

state.condition: If other labs adopt similar protocols

events.title: Defines ML R&D acceleration and automation levels
events.summary: Version 3.1 sets levels for substantial acceleration of AI progress and for full automation of any Google AI research team. It aims to share information with governments when a level poses material risk.

quote.text: Can fully automate the work of any team of researchers at Google focused on improving AI capabilities, with approximately comparable all-inclusive costs.

state.condition: If other labs adopt similar protocols

events.title: Reports holistic assessment of ML R&D automation
events.summary: The Gemini 4 Argon report adds an assessment of how far ML R&D is automated inside Google DeepMind, and reports that the model does not reach the ML R&D levels.

quote.text: A holistic assessment of the degree of ML R&D automation within Google DeepMind.

state.condition: If other labs adopt similar protocols

threshold.commitment: FSF 3.1 sets ML R&D levels; Gemini 4 report assesses internal automation.

safeguards-first.commitment: Safety case required before external or high-risk internal deployment.

human-oversight.missing: No rule found that humans approve key steps when models do AI research.

disclosure.commitment: Aims to share information with governments when a level poses material risk.
disclosure.missing: Only an aim; no public notice pledge.

orgs.summary: Meta evaluates autonomous AI R&D under its Loss of Control domain and plans to track research automation. Its CEO backs competitive RSI investment.

events.title: Adds autonomous AI R&D to Loss of Control
events.summary: Version 2 evaluates whether models can do the work of a senior research engineer improving AI, or speed AI progress well beyond historical rates. Development continues only with validated safeguards.

quote.text: Autonomously complete research tasks which are representative of the work of a senior research engineer improving AI capabilities at Meta, and/or results in AI progress substantially accelerating from historical rates.

sources.title: Scaling how we build and test our most advanced AI

events.title: CEO backs RSI compute to stay competitive
events.summary: Zuckerberg says labs should allot enough compute to recursive self-improvement to stay competitive, keep most compute for people's goals, and coordinate if AI shows harmful behavior.

quote.text: All labs should observe its objectives and our ability to control them carefully, and if there is any indication of harmful behavior then we should coordinate and adjust appropriately.

events.title: Adds human control measures for model development
events.summary: Version 2.1 adds training-run monitoring and measures to keep humans in control of model development. It plans to track how autonomous research changes the rate of AI progress.

quote.text: Establishing mechanisms for tracking the impact of autonomous research capabilities on the rate of AI progress.

threshold.commitment: Evaluates senior research engineer tasks and accelerated AI progress under Loss of Control.

safeguards-first.commitment: Past critical, develops only with validated mitigations.
safeguards-first.missing: No stop past the critical threshold.

human-oversight.commitment: Adds training monitors and measures to keep humans in control of development.
human-oversight.missing: No rule found that humans approve key steps.

disclosure.commitment: Plans to track how autonomous research changes AI progress.
disclosure.missing: No pledge found to tell the public or governments.

orgs.summary: xAI removed its listed AI R&D automation metrics in June 2026. Its current framework sets no automated research threshold.

events.title: Lists AI R&D automation metrics it may publish
events.summary: The Risk Management Framework says xAI may publish the share of its code or pull requests that its models write, or other metrics of AI R&D automation. It sets no AI R&D threshold.

quote.text: Internal AI usage: Assess the percent of code or percent of pull requests at xAI generated by our models, or other potential metrics related to AI research and development automation.

events.title: Removes AI R&D automation metrics from framework
events.summary: The rewritten framework no longer lists the internal AI usage metrics or other transparency provisions.

sources.title: xAI Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework (effective 30 June 2026)

threshold.missing: No AI R&D threshold in the 2025 or June 2026 framework.

safeguards-first.missing: No safeguards tied to automated AI research in any framework version.

human-oversight.missing: No rule found that humans approve key steps; no oversight body named.

disclosure.missing: June 2026 rewrite removed the 2025 AI R&D automation metrics.

orgs.summary: Microsoft defines a critical level for full AI R&D automation that needs further review and mitigations, and commits to pause if risk cannot be mitigated.

events.title: Sets critical level for full AI R&D automation
events.summary: The Frontier Governance Framework tracks advanced autonomy, including AI R&D. At the critical level, a model can fully automate the AI R&D pipeline, and further review and mitigations are required.

quote.text: The model can fully automate the AI R&D pipeline at a fraction of human labor costs, majorly accelerating AI R&D.

events.title: Adds loss of control as a tracked capability
events.summary: The revised framework adds loss of control and harmful manipulation. It says Microsoft is still researching how to evaluate loss of control risk and set acceptance criteria.

quote.text: We are researching approaches to evaluating models for loss of control risk in a pre-deployment context and setting appropriate risk acceptance criteria for this tracked high-risk capability.

threshold.commitment: Critical is full AI R&D automation, found by leading indicator and deeper assessments.

safeguards-first.commitment: Critical requires review and mitigations; pauses if risk cannot be mitigated.

human-oversight.missing: No rule found that humans approve key steps; loss of control evaluation still in research.

disclosure.commitment: Publishes model risk classifications and evaluations.
disclosure.missing: No pledge found to report when AI does most research.
